title: How are macOS and Linux each qualified for launch?
body: You chose Linux and macOS. All adapter evidence so far is Linux-only, and macOS adds launchd, a different PTY/terminal stack, and its own provider CLI builds. Options: (A) Both are launch platforms. Neither is certified until its own qualification run passes, so launch waits for both. (B) Launch certifies Linux first, and macOS ships in v1 as soon as it passes the same qualification, without holding Linux back. (C) macOS is best-effort and uncertified.
rec: B. Both are v1 platforms held to one qualification bar, and certification is per platform, so macOS can lag Linux without blocking it. An uncertified platform refuses to start agents, with actionable guidance, under the existing 'reject unsupported combinations' rule.
options: B: per-platform certification, Linux may lead

title: How does the daemon start, and does it come back after a reboot by itself?
body: Options: (A) Only explicitly. `asmai start` runs the daemon, and after a reboot the factory stays down until you start it again. (B) `asmai start` by default, plus an opt-in `asmai service install` that registers a systemd user unit (with linger, so it runs without a login on remote Linux) or a launchd LaunchAgent, so it auto-starts after a reboot. (C) Always installed as a login/boot service.
rec: B. The daemon works without any service manager, and the service is opt-in. Either way, every start runs the same recovery: restore leaders, then reconcile. The macOS LaunchAgent starts at login, not at boot, which is acceptable for v1.
options: B: explicit start + opt-in service install

title: What happens when an agent's provider process dies unexpectedly?
body: The daemon survived, but a leader or worker CLI exited or crashed. Options: (A) The daemon restarts it automatically on the same provider, resuming the native session where possible, with bounded retries and backoff before escalating. (B) Leaders restart automatically. A dead worker is not restarted: its assignment becomes 'needs reconciliation' and its owning leader decides whether to re-dispatch, to the same or a fresh worker, after checking effects. (C) Nothing restarts automatically, and every case asks you.
rec: B. Leaders are restarted automatically on the same provider, which the earlier decision already allows. After a few failed restarts in a short window, the role pauses and Coordination tells you. If Coordination itself cannot be restored, `asmai status` reports it. Worker recovery is a decision for the owning leader, never a blind retry.
options: B: auto-restart leaders; owning leader handles dead workers

title: What does stopping the factory do?
body: Options: (A) Drain. `asmai stop` dispatches nothing new, lets running turns reach a boundary (waiting, stopped, or result) up to a timeout, then interrupts the rest, persists state, and exits. Interrupted work becomes 'needs reconciliation' at the next start. `asmai stop --now` skips the wait. (B) Always immediate: terminate everything and reconcile at the next start.
rec: A. Drain with a timeout, plus `--now`. Pending human decisions, grants, and queued requests persist across the stop. Both a stop and a host shutdown that is not a clean stop recover through the same reconciliation path.

title: When you attach to a working agent, how do you take the keyboard?
body: The adapter decision requires one input owner, takeover at a known boundary, and an explicit release. Open questions: is attach read-only by default, and what happens when the agent is mid-turn? Options: (A) Attach observes by default. Taking input is a separate explicit action. If a turn is running, you choose to wait for its boundary (the default) or interrupt it now. Any unsent automated draft is recorded and cleared before you get the keyboard. (B) Attach always takes input immediately and interrupts any running turn. (C) Attach takes input but queues your keystrokes until the turn finishes.
rec: A. Observe by default, take control explicitly, wait for the boundary by default with interrupt as an option, and clear the draft with a record. Native permission prompts are already a boundary, so you can answer them directly. Detaching without releasing leaves automation paused, as already decided.
options: A: observe by default; explicit take; wait-or-interrupt

title: How are AsmAI and provider CLI upgrades applied?
body: Options: (A) No hot upgrade. Upgrading AsmAI requires a drained stop and then a start. At start, the daemon checks the provider CLI versions and refuses unqualified combinations before dispatching anything. (B) AsmAI may hot-swap the daemon while agents keep running.
rec: A. Upgrade between a stop and a start, and validate versions at start. If a provider CLI upgrades itself while the factory runs, affected agents pause at their next restart until the combination is qualified. The installation mechanism and package format stay with the CLI setup and packaging tickets.
